the optimization of ferric chloride concentrations and pH values in microalgae culture media is a good strategy to improve both microalgae biomass growth and flocculability.

the integrated bioprocess allows to achieve high cell growth rates, to improve microalgae flocculation and to reduce the medium requirements for a sustainable and cost effective production of microalgae.

the optimization of the medium conditions and with the reuse of the culture medium.

the development of a novel integrated bioprocess to improve both the microalgae cultivation efficiency and the microalgae harvesting efficiency, and to reduce the production costs of microalgae biomass.
the optimization of a continuous microalgae cultivation process, which is a key step for the industrial development of microalgae.

the integrated bioprocess is feasible and can be considered as a potential alternative for the production of biofuels.
the integrated bioprocess conceived as a sole-step, in continuous mode, and with the reuse of clarified medium recovered, would be a promising alternative for the production of microalgae biomass.
the use of ferric chloride to induce flocculation in microalgal cultures is a very promising strategy for microalgae production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a sole step bioprocess for the cultivation of microalgae and the recovery of biomass can be successfully implemented in continuous operation mode, and that medium reuse is a feasible strategy to reduce the production costs.
we have demonstrated that a continuous integrated bioprocess can be run for the cultivation and harvesting of microalgae.
the integrated bioprocess can be operated continuously and that the reuse of clarified medium is possible.

the reuse of the medium in a continuous bioprocess can be successfully performed without any nutrient addition.
the reuse of the medium recovered from microalgae cultivation in a photobioreactor is possible without any further nutrient addition.
